topIssues.title: op-reth proofs history can lag permanently after clean shutdown
topIssues.author: HDauven
topIssues.body:
### Description

With `op-reth v2.4.0` and v2 proofs history enabled, a clean SIGTERM can leave the persisted proofs window behind the execution-chain tip. On restart the gap is permanent: ExEx notifications for the missing blocks are not replayed, `proofs init` is a no-op for an initialized store and `debug_proofsSyncStatus.latest` remains below `eth_blockNumber`. Rebuilding the proofs store from the chain DB repairs it.

### Reproduction

1. Initialize v2 proofs history and run op-reth with `--proofs-history` while an op-node sequencer produces blocks.
2. Observe a small live lag, for example execution tip `3642` and persisted proof latest `3640`.
3. Send SIGTERM and wait for op-reth to exit cleanly.
4. Restart against the same execution DB and proofs DB.
5. The execution tip remains `3642`, while `debug_proofsSyncStatus.latest` remains `3640` indefinitely. Running `op-reth proofs init` does not advance it because the store is already initialized.

This was reproduced with the official `op-reth:v2.4.0` image. The same shutdown path is still present on current `develop`.

### Suspected cause

`OpProofsExEx::handle_notification` emits `ExExEvent::FinishedHeight` after the collector action returns, but that action only buffers the block; persistence happens asynchronously and below-threshold blocks can remain in memory. The engine shutdown path drains only an already in-flight save and does not schedule the remaining memory buffer for persistence. The ExEx WAL therefore considers those notifications finished even though their proof state was never persisted.

Relevant code:

- `rust/op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs`: `FinishedHeight` is emitted after queueing collector work.
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/runner.rs`: shutdown calls only `drain_persistence()`.
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/state.rs`: `drain_persistence()` waits for an existing save but does not start one for buffered blocks.

### Expected behavior

A clean shutdown should persist all buffered proof-history blocks before the collector exits and before a completed ExEx height can become unrecoverable. A regression test should cover shutdown with fewer buffered blocks than the persistence threshold and verify that the restarted proof window reaches the execution tip.

topPRs.title: docs: regenerate op-reth CLI reference at v2.4.1 via new gen-op-reth-cli pipeline (IA slice 9)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

IA-modernization slice 9 (final slice of the lane) per [`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md): the op-reth CLI regeneration pipeline, plus its first regeneration at `op-reth/v2.4.1`.

## Before / After

**Before:** the 59-page op-reth CLI reference was a one-time snapshot of the retired Vocs site with no regeneration pipeline. It silently drifted from every op-reth release — missing whole command families (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`), documenting seven `db settings set` subcommands the binary no longer has, and carrying stale flags and help text on 51 pages.

**After:** the reference is regenerated from the current finalized release (`op-reth/v2.4.1`) and gains a documented, review-gated regeneration pipeline for future releases. Readers get 21 new command pages (including the whole `proofs` family), 51 corrected pages, and the 7 retired pages redirect to the surviving `db settings set` page that documents the replacement `v2` flow. The hand-written CLI overview gains one table row (`proofs`).

## How

- **Pipeline** — new `docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/` (`main.mjs` + `README.md` + `manifest.json`): a zero-dependency Node port of upstream reth's `docs/cli/update.sh` + `docs/cli/help.rs` (the exact tooling whose output format the original snapshot matches). It walks a pinned release binary's `--help` tree and emits the MDX pages (`diataxis: reference` frontmatter), the docs.json nav fragment for the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group (hand-written `cli/overview` guarded as the group's first entry, never touched), and provenance in `manifest.json`. Environment-dependent help output (home paths, version/target triples, CPU-count defaults) is scrubbed with upstream's replacement set.
- **Provenance chain** — binary built from source at tag `op-reth/v2.4.1` (tag commit `a9a8dad3f15`, the latest finalized non-rc release), which pins upstream reth at rev `f2eecc65482a`. `manifest.json` records `{tag, binaryVersion, sha256-over-generated-tree}`.
- **Idempotency** — running the generator twice against the same binary is a byte-for-byte no-op (verified live: second run reports `0 new, 0 changed, removed 0`, `git status` clean). `--check` mode recomputes the whole tree in memory and fails on any divergence, so hand edits to generated pages cannot survive review.

## No CI wiring (per Matthew's ruling)

Nothing in this diff touches `.circleci/`, `.github/`, or any package script; nothing runs unattended. Regeneration is registered as a **review-gated Mintlify docs automation** (see the README's "Automation registration" section, mirroring the gen-flags precedent in `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`): when a newer finalized `op-reth/v*` tag exists than the manifest's, a regeneration is *proposed for human review* — never merged by CI. All 79 changed files live under `docs/public-docs/`.

## Regeneration drift (first run at v2.4.1)

| Kind | Count | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New pages | 21 | `proofs` family (7 pages), `db copy`, `db migrate-v2`, `db state`, `db prune-checkpoints` (3), `db stage-checkpoints` (3), `db checksum rocksdb`, `db get rocksdb`, `db settings set v2`, `p2p enode` |
| Updated pages | 51 | Genuine drift: new flags (e.g. `--tx-channel-memory-limit`, `--rpc.disable-metrics`, `--rpc-cache.max-bals`), renames (`--enable-discv5-discovery` → `--disable-discv5-discovery`), help-text and `--chain` list changes |
| Deleted pages | 7 | The per-table `db settings set <table>` leaves, superseded upstream by `db settings set v2` |
| Nav entries | 409 → 423 | +21 / −7; all other tabs and groups byte-identical, tab count 8 → 8 |

## Redirects (645 → 652)

| Change | Count | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (R5, one per deleted page) | 7 | `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/db/settings/set/<table>` → `.../db/settings/set` (the surviving parent documenting the `v2` flow) |
| Retargeted in place | 9 | The legacy `/rust/op-reth/cli/.../db/settings/set/<table>` entries (7 + 2 `*_in_static_files`) each pointed at a now-deleted URL; retargeted to `.../db/settings/set` so no chains or stale destinations exist |

Full 652-entry trace: 0 duplicate sources, 0 chains, 0 sources shadowing live pages, 0 destinations pointing at deleted URLs; no prose page links to any deleted URL.

## Deviations from the plan (stated plainly)

1. **7 redirects vs the plan's ~0–5 budget** — the estimate predates further months of upstream drift; every removal is the single superseded `db settings set` per-table family, all covered same-PR per R5 (plus the 9 in-place retargets the no-chain rule requires).
2. **Binary built from source (dev profile) instead of the release Docker image** — the release ships no binary assets and the image registry is egress-blocked in the build environment. Feature set matches the official image build (default features = DockerfileOp set); clap `--help` output is feature-dependent, not profile-dependent. Release metadata was injected exactly as the official image build does.
3. **One fork-specific scrub beyond upstream `help.rs`** — `default: op-reth/<VERSION>-<SHA>/<ARCH>`: the fork identifies as `op-reth/...` where upstream's scrub patterns only cover the `reth/...` spelling; without it the build-host arch would leak into a page. Recorded in `main.mjs` comments and the README.
4. **`manifest.json` carries `binaryVersion`** in addition to the gen-flags-precedent `{tag, sha256}` — extra provenance for a binary-derived generator.

## Verification (re-derived independently by the verifier)

- `--check` against the tag binary: exit 0 — 72 pages, nav fragment, and manifest all match the `--help` tree; manifest sha256 `e979848d9b4a…9017f6ad` re-derived independently and matches.
- `op-reth/v2.4.1` confirmed as the latest finalized (non-rc, non-draft) op-reth release via the GitHub API; `rust/Cargo.toml` at the tag pins reth rev `f2eecc65482a`.
- Sample pages (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`, `node`, `db list`, `config`): flag sets match the binary's `--help` exactly; the 7 deleted commands are absent from the binary (`db settings set` now has only `v2`).
- Leakage sweep over all 72 pages: zero hits for the version string, commit SHAs, build timestamps, target triples, or build-host paths.
- Lints: `validate-nav.ts` OK (424 pages on disk / 423 nav entries / 1 allowlisted orphan — counts reconcile exactly), `validate-redirects.ts` OK (652 redirects, 11 grandfathered — baseline byte-identical to how IA-8 left it), `lint-link-policy.mjs` 0 findings. All 73 touched MDX files compile clean under @mdx-js/mdx.

## Wiz SAST findings (8 LOW) — addressed

Wiz flagged 8 LOW SAST findings on the PR head. The only SAST-scannable code in this diff is `scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/main.mjs` (everything else is MDX/JSON/Markdown), and its sinks account for exactly the two pattern classes Wiz LOW-flags in JavaScript: two `child_process` executions (`execFileSync` for `--help`/`--version`) and six dynamic-path `fs` operations (page write/mkdir/delete, docs.json write, manifest read/write, existing-page reads).

Context: this is a repo-local, review-gated generator that only shells out to a binary the operator explicitly passes via `--bin` (built locally from a release tag); it already used `execFileSync` with argument arrays (no shell), and every dynamic path is rooted at script-relative constants. The one genuine untrusted-input flow — subcommand names parsed from the binary's `--help` output feed both process arguments and file paths — is now hardened in `06bcbc29c9`: names are validated against the shape clap actually produces (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/`, run aborts on anything else), and every page write/delete asserts containment inside the generated tree. No behavior change: `--check` still passes byte-identically at v2.4.1. The remaining dynamic-path reads/writes against script-relative constants (docs.json, manifest.json) are inherent to any generator and not reachable from untrusted input.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Preview: the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group under Node Operators → Reference renders with `overview` first and nested subgroups in `--help` order (eyeball `db settings set` → `set`, `v2`)
- [ ] Spot-check a new page (e.g. `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/proofs`) against `op-reth proofs --help` at v2.4.1
- [ ] Hit a deleted URL (e.g. `.../db/settings/set/receipts`) and confirm the redirect lands on `.../db/settings/set`
- [ ] Confirm the README's automation-registration section matches the intended Mintlify registry entry (review-gated, never CI)
- [ ] Agree the 4 deviations above are acceptable

## Program status

This closes the IA-modernization lane: slices 1–9 have all shipped. D12 is the program's last remaining content slice.

topPRs.title: op-dispute-mon: monitor ZK dispute games
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Closes #18424.

Related scope: #18323.

## Why

ZK dispute games are supported by the lifecycle scheduler but were invisible to `op-dispute-mon`, whose extraction and downstream monitors assumed fault-game state. This adds native, pinned ZK monitoring without changing contracts, flags, runtime gates, or bond lifecycle behavior.

ZK, fault, and SuperPermissioned games now contribute to the existing aggregate `op_dispute_mon_games_agreement` totals. The metric retains its historical `status`, `completion`, `result_correctness`, and `root_agreement` labels and its eight canonical series. Per-type visibility remains available through `op_dispute_mon_games{game_type=...}`.

A canonical ZK child forced to a challenger result by an invalid parent still agrees with the reference root. Its `agree_challenger_ahead` or `agree_challenger_wins` series is therefore classified as `incorrect`, preserving the historical deterministic correctness semantics.

## Testing

- `cd op-dispute-mon && mise exec -- just test`
- `mise exec -- go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts/... ./op-challenger/game/zk/... ./op-dispute-mon/... ./op-devstack/dsl/disputemon/... -count=1`
- `RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 mise exec -- go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk/... -run ^TestZKDisputeMonitor -count=1 -v`
- `mise exec -- just lint-go`

The full `mise exec -- just go-tests` gate was also attempted. The changed packages passed, but the overall local run failed in unrelated setup-dependent packages because `cannon/testdata/bin/hello.64.elf` and `forge-artifacts/artifacts.tzst` were absent and `MAINNET_RPC_URL`/`SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` were unset. `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` also timed out with `context deadline exceeded` in the full run and package rerun, then passed when retried alone.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: continue prepared chain deployments
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `op-deployer continue` for prepared deployments. `prepare` now snapshots its canonical intent, predicted addresses, deployer, OPCM, anchor timing, and contract artifact digests. `continue` uses that snapshot as its authority and rejects drift before execution.

All pending chains are simulated and verified before any transaction. Each send rechecks the anchor and deployer nonce, checkpoints the chain only after a canonical receipt, and verifies live configuration from one L1 block.

Retries reconcile complete deployments, reject partial deployments, and redeploy a checkpointed chain only when its deployment disappeared while the prepared anchor remains valid.

**Tests**

Covers prepared-input and artifact drift, all-chain preflight, broadcast guards, exact configuration checks, retries, reconciliation, reorg recovery, the full workflow, and the CLI.

**Additional context**

Stacked on #21897. The starting anchor proposal and prestate remain in chain state because they are derived after address prediction. Other continuation inputs cannot silently diverge from the prediction, including across retries after chain state is normalized.

Across multiple chains, independent L1 transactions cannot be atomic. A later failure leaves completed chains checkpointed for retry.

**Metadata**

Closes #21669

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: defend challenged games with SP1 super-aggregation proofs
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Ports the defend path from op-succinct's `fault-proof` proposer (@ `13716c2c`): when a game the proposer can prove gets challenged, it fetches the span's super roots, collects witnesses, obtains an SP1 super-aggregation proof bound to its signer, and submits `prove()`. The existing resolution and claim tasks then finish the game (including the challenger-bond prover credit).

Part of #21463. Fast finality (prove at creation) is deliberately not ported; tracked in #22112. Stacked on #22097.

## What is upstream and what is ours

- Ported near-verbatim (diff against upstream side by side): `prover.rs` (SPN request/poll state machine; cluster arm and two request knobs dropped), the defense scheduling in `proposer.rs` (`spawn_game_defense_tasks`, `should_skip_proving`, `spawn_game_proving_task`, deadline tiers), `RangeSplitCount`.
- Ours by necessity (no upstream analog): `proving.rs` replaces upstream's single-chain witness/stdin machinery with the super-root stack (`super-range-executor` witness collection, `SuperAggregationInputs`); `synthesize_execution` generalized to timestamp spans (host-side only, no vkey change); the multi-prestate `PrestateCache` gains per-prestate proving keys and the deferred vkey verification (agg vk must hash to the on-chain prestate).
- Ownership is now prestate-based (option A, #22111): the proposer proves, resolves, and claims every game whose prestate artifacts it can load, regardless of creator. Prove set = resolve set = claim set.

## No real proofs in this PR

There are no SPN calls and no SNARK cryptography in any test. All coverage runs the mock provider: submitted proof bytes are a placeholder constant and devstack's `ZKMockVerifier` accepts any bytes. What the tests exercise for real is every computation around the proof: span fetching, witness collection from live nodes, native re-derivation of the state transition (the same code the guest programs compile from), consolidation checks, aggregation-input validation, and the exact public-values tuple `prove()` reconstructs on-chain. The one unexercised seam, `generate_*_proof()` returning verifier-accepted bytes, is upstream's code nearly verbatim and gets a manual SPN smoke once credentials are provisioned.

## Hardening beyond upstream

Two serious issues caught in pre-merge review, fixed with pinning unit tests. Neither exists upstream; both are invariants upstream gets structurally for free that our architectural departures initially violated:

1. Permanent verdicts are trust-gated: the `undefendable` skip set (added to bound retry spend; upstream retries forever) only condemns a game on a supernode answer with `current_l1 >= verified_required_l1`. Without the gate, a mid-rewind stale answer could permanently mark an honest game undefendable and burn its bond.
2. Poisoned prestates close the creation gate: upstream verifies embedded ELF vkeys before creating; our runtime-fetched artifacts verify at first key setup, which initially left the existence-only gate open, letting the proposer keep bonding games it had proven it cannot defend. `ensure_loaded` now returns false for poisoned entries and heals only when the published artifacts actually change.

Smaller deliberate divergences, flagged inline: pre-submit re-check before the prove tx (upstream submits blind), sync loads every cached game's prestate so post-rotation games stay owned (upstream is single-identity), mock provider is native-core rather than emulator-based (stub artifacts are not ELFs).

## Test plan

- Rust: 84 unit tests (proposer + super-range-executor) incl. ported upstream tables, six migrated span tests, and the two hardening pins; clippy `--all-features --all-targets --locked` and `just lint-docs` clean.
- Go: gofmt/vet/op-golangci-lint clean.
- Acceptance (sysgo, stub mode, PR CI lane): full ZK suite 10/10, incl. `TestChallengedValidProposalAnchors` now proposer-driven (the `TODO(#21463)` flip) and new `TestProposerDefendsForeignValidGame` pinning option A end to end (foreign game proven, resolved, challenger bond claimed).
- Real-ELF lane: `TestChallengedValidProposalAnchors` + `TestProposerClaimsBondAfterResolution` pass with real artifacts.
- `TestZKDisputeGameWithdrawal` stays skipped: its single-chain preset fails bring-up installing the ZK game type (pre-existing, unrelated to the proposer; issue to follow).
